newsitem.title: USA: Weather leaves New Englanders in the dark.
newsitem.headline: Weather leaves New Englanders in the dark.

text.p: Thousands of New England residents spent Sunday without electricity because of a furious storm that dumped more than 18 inches of heavy wet snow on some communities, officials said.

Amtrak was forced to cancel its "Vermonter" passenger train and put passengers on buses Sunday after the storm washed out a 100-foot section of track owned by the New England Central Railroad in Claremont, N.H., the railroad said.

Emergency utility crews were called out in Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island, New Hampshire and Maine, with officials warning some customers may have to wait until Monday or Tuesday to get service restored.

The storm blanketed inland communities with snow while soaking those on the coast with driving rain. Jaffrey, N.H. received 17 inches of snow and South Bridgton, Maine 14 inches, according to the National Weather Service.

"MassElectric reports that they have about 120,000 customers without power, Boston Edison says they have 20,000 and in the western part of the state there are another 20,000," said Jerry Meister, director of operations for the Massachusetts Emergency Management Agency.
Meister said that while Boston Edison expected to restore service to its customers by the end of the day, it would be late Monday or Tuesday before MassElectric's customers would be fully restored.

Central Maine Power Co reported more than 40,000 customers without electricity Sunday afternoon in western and southern areas of the state. More than 60,000 had lost electricity at the height of the storm, the company said.

In Connecticut, more than 100,000 were without power for many hours beginning late on Saturday due mainly to the heavy snow pulling down wires. Most were back on line by midday Sunday but some were expected to be without power until Monday.
Storm continued to drop snow and light rain on northern Maine Sunday as it headed in to the Canadian Maritime provinces where forecasters warned residents to expect rain and heavy winds.
